title: Interplay of spin-orbit coupling and magnetic chirality: Multidirectional spin polarization in a helical antiferromagnet
authors: Kallol Mondal, Sudin Ganguly, Santanu K. Maiti
abstract: We investigate spin-dependent transport in a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet in the presence of spin-orbit coupling within a tight-binding framework. Using the Landauer-Büttiker formalism, we analyze the generation of spin polarization arising from the combined effects of the helical magnetic texture and spin-orbit interaction. We find that finite spin polarization can be generated simultaneously along the $\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$-directions, in contrast to the predominantly single-axis spin polarization commonly observed in conventional spin-filtering systems. The multidirectional spin polarization originates from the symmetry breaking introduced by the non-collinear magnetic order. We further show that the spin polarization is modified significantly in the presence of spin-orbit coupling and it has strong dependence on the parameters associated with the helical system. In particular, long-range hopping significantly enhances the spin-filtering effect, leading to large spin polarization components along all three spatial directions.
summary: This theoretical study models spin transport through a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet incorporating spin-orbit coupling. Using the Landauer-Büttiker formalism, the authors demonstrate that the helical structure generates unique, multidirectional spin polarization components. The results highlight that structural chirality and long-range hopping are key parameters for achieving highly tunable spin-filtering effects.
main_problem: The study investigates spin-dependent transport in a non-collinear helical antiferromagnet subjected to spin-orbit coupling (SOC). The goal is to understand how this interplay generates spin polarization.
main_result: The system exhibits robust, multidirectional spin polarization ($\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z}$), which is significantly enhanced by long-range hopping and arises from the symmetry breaking inherent in the non-collinear magnetic texture.
method: The analysis employs the Landauer-Büttiker formalism combined with the Green's function approach to calculate spin-resolved transmission probabilities and currents.
model_or_system: The model is a tight-binding description of a single-stranded non-collinear antiferromagnetic helix coupled to semi-infinite 1D leads. The Hamiltonian incorporates spin-dependent scattering, electron hopping, and SOC.
key_observables: Spin polarization components ($P_x, P_y, P_z$), spin-polarized electrical currents, and spin-dependent transmission probabilities ($T_{\sigma\sigma'}$).
important_parameters: Helical parameters like radius ($R$), stacking distance ($\Delta z$), and twisting angle ($\Delta\phi$); SOC strength ($t_{so}$); Fermi energy ($E_F$); and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the coherent transport regime, without invoking dephasing mechanisms, and often assumes a uniform magnitude for the spin-dependent scattering field.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of spin polarization on SOC strength vs. Fermi energy (Fig. 9), the bias voltage dependence for various twisting angles (Fig. 10), and the temperature dependence up to 500 K (Fig. 11).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the transport properties by first establishing the model Hamiltonian and then applying the Landauer-Büttiker formalism. It progresses by demonstrating the emergence of multidirectional polarization, showing its tunability via structural chirality ($\Delta\phi$), and finally confirming its robustness across varying external parameters like SOC strength and temperature.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and spintronics, as it models spin transport in geometrically constrained magnetic materials, providing theoretical predictions for novel spin-filtering effects beyond simple collinear systems.

Successive magnetic mo- ments (shown with the 3D arrows associated with red balls) are progressively rotated with respect to one another, giving rise to a chiral magnetic texture with vanishing net magneti- zation. In the transport setup, the source and drain leads are attached to the end sites, denoted with 1 and N, respectively. The leads are omitted from the ﬁgure for clarity.

FIG. 2. (Color online). Energy dependence of the spin-resolved transmission probabilities T ↑(↓) α (α = x, y, z) for the short-range hopping (SRH) helix with N = 20, tso = 0.25, and h = 0.5. Panels (a), (b), and (c) correspond to the x, y, and z-directions, respectively. In each panel, the red (black) curves represent the spin-up (spin-down) transmission probabilities.

FIG. 3. (Color online). Spin-resolved current components I↑(↓) α (α = x, y, z) as a function of the applied bias voltage for the SRH conﬁguration, shown in panels (a), (b), and (c), respectively. The red and black curves correspond to the up- and down-spin currents. All data are computed for a ﬁxed Fermi energy EF = 0.5 eV. The system parameters are the same as Fig. 2.
